text: — In eighteen fifty-nine, a bankrupt man walks into a San Francisco newspaper with an announcement.
I declare myself Emperor of these United States.
The editor prints it as a joke. But the whole city decides to play along.
His name is Joshua Norton. He was rich once, until he bet everything on a shipload of rice, and lost it all.
Now he walks the streets in a blue uniform, with a sword and a feathered hat.
Every day, he inspects his city. The sidewalks. The streetcars. The police.
He prints his own money, and some shops accept it.
Even the census lists his job as Emperor.
Then, in eighteen sixty-seven, a policeman arrests him, calling him insane.
The city is furious. The police chief frees him, and apologizes.
After that, policemen salute him in the street.
In eighteen seventy-two, he orders a bridge built across the bay. Nobody listens.
In eighteen eighty, he dies with almost nothing.
Ten thousand people come to say goodbye.
And that bridge he ordered? It opened in nineteen thirty-six.
